messages.subject: zero inflated type2
parts:
Hi
When do we use zero-inflated Poisson type2? I have read zeroinflated.pdf  but I need explain more about type2.

messages.author: d560d9e01924933c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] zero inflated type2
parts:
Hi,

I am sorry, I have replied only to you. I am including it in the list again because I am not able to answer you properly.

So, you are probably right, the advanced example in page 9 is a mixture of a degenerate distribution {P(Y=0)=1} with a truncated Poisson {P(Y=y | Y > 0)}, (type 0 model) and you are able to add a linear term to the zero-inflated probability using the clever trick of two likelihoods described in the example.

The type 2 (page 10) seems to be another thing, where instead of having the zero-inflated probability directly as type 1 model, you have the alpha parameter, you also have x which I am not sure exactly how you can add the linear term.

Cheers,
Leo

Dear Leo Bastos

Thank you for your response. I think it adds a linear predictor to the zero-probability in the type 1 model. Please see page 10.

If we use type2 in a spatial model, what is linear predictor to the zero-probability? Please give me a brief explanation about x. (Is x a independent variable, covariate or ..?)


best regards

Zero-inflated type 2 is a clever trick to add a linear predictor to

I hope it helps.
